mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, which results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) over three months signals a strong demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST showed a sustained increase over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within two months signals a contraction in supply, leading to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO decreased by more than 1% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it indicates inflationary pressure coupled with high borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: high inflation with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS was above 3% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.2% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two quarters signals strong economic growth, which leads to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where GDPC1 showed a sustained increase over two quarters.

mechanism_narrative: When the industrial production index (INDPRO) increases by more than 2% in a quarter and real GDP (GDPC1) also increases by more than 1% in the same period, it indicates a strong supply-side expansion, leading to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases > 2% and GDPC1 increases > 1% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 2% and GDPC1 increased by more than 1% in the same quarter.
